section.linux-notes.title: Linux notes
section.linux-notes.sub: Watchdog, Workshop, mods, ports and community VPS notes.
section.linux-notes.b0.0: From the official Co-op Discord setup, FAQ and Linux notes, reviewed 6 November 2026. Treat a community recipe as unverified unless this page says it was tested.
section.linux-notes.b1.d0.b0.0: Workshop item 3770450698 includes DedicatedServer/BannerlordCoopServer.exe at steamapps/workshop/content/261550/3770450698/. For a manual install, extract the matching client so Modules/Coop/SubModule.xml exists. For a first test, enable only Co-op, turn other mods and War Sails off, and answer No to Safe Mode. Do not enable a manual Modules/Coop folder and the Workshop module together. If you switch, back up and remove the extra copy. Workshop updates wait on TaleWorlds and can lag the release, so compare versions.
section.linux-notes.b1.summary.0: Use Workshop or a manual copy, not both
section.linux-notes.b2.d0.b0.0: Launch the client through Steam. If you see SteamAPI_Init failed, restart Steam only after you confirm no running server depends on it. Do not change a live game or server while you test.
section.linux-notes.b2.summary.0: Start the Linux client from Steam
section.linux-notes.b3.d0.b0.0: Discord reports say renaming bin/Win64_Shipping_Client/watchdog can reduce world-map stutter on Bazzite, CachyOS and Arch. The developers warn that crash logs then cannot be sent for support. Do this only with permission, while the game is closed, and keep the backup so you can restore it. --no-watchdog is a server argument, not a client option. See https://github.com/Bannerlord-Coop-Team/BannerlordCoop/issues/2536.
section.linux-notes.b3.summary.0: Watchdog stutter: rename the folder, do not delete it
section.linux-notes.b4.d0.b0.0: Add BannerlordCoopServer.exe as a non-Steam game, choose GE-Proton, and put --no-watchdog in the server launch options. Or use the game's Proton prefix. For a test, use a separate prefix and --data-dir. Do not point a test at a live server's prefix or saves. A Steam lobby under Proton or Wine is still unverified. Use direct IP when you need a result you can repeat.
section.linux-notes.b5.d0.b0.0: Set steam:false in server-config.json. Allow UDP 4200–4201 on the host, the router and any cloud firewall. The main port defaults to 4200. A player-hosted Steam invite can skip port forwarding and CGNAT. Do not assume a dedicated server under Proton or Wine can. Turn off a conflicting VPN or DNS tool only after you check sessions that still need it.
section.linux-notes.b6.d0.b0.0: Difficulty and gameplay settings are in CoopData/mod-config.json. Connection settings are in CoopData/DedicatedServer/server-config.json. A Workshop layout may use DedicatedServer/server-data/mod-config.json. Read the paths printed at startup, then stop only that server before you edit. battleSize defaults to 1000; about 400 is easier on the CPU. Other keys: autoPauseEnabled, goldFoodInfluenceChangeInSettlements, enablePlayerExecutions, enableHeroExecutions, birthAndDeath, clanMemberDeathChance and battleDeath. Keep the separate Birth and Aging module off.
section.linux-notes.b7.d0.b0.0: Confirm Co-op works by itself first. Copy a compatible mod into engine/Modules. The folder name must match the mod Id. In the server UI, reload, enable the mod, set the load order, choose Save Mods, then restart only that server. Every player needs the same mods, versions and order. Discord reports say War Sails, Birth and Aging Options and Fast Mode do not work on dedicated servers. Do not change Steam subscriptions from a script.
section.linux-notes.b7.summary.0: Add mods only after Co-op works alone
section.linux-notes.b8.d0.b0.0: Server log: CoopData/DedicatedServer/logs/coop-server-{date}-{time}.log. Client log: bin/Win64_Shipping_Client/Coop_client.log. In-game host log: Coop_server.log. Linux paths are case-sensitive. Crashes may be under the prefix's drive_c/ProgramData/Mount and Blade II Bannerlord/crashes or Documents/Mount and Blade II Bannerlord/Coop Crash Reports. Keep the crash report, because Send can delete it. Remove secrets, then use the official support channel. Do not keep rejoining a stalled session.
section.linux-notes.b9.d0.b0.0: A headless server reached SERVING here with WineHQ Wine 11.0 (docker.io/tianon/wine:11.0.0, winehq-stable 11.0.0 on Debian trixie) plus Xvfb. Debian's stock Wine 8.0 failed the same steps: virtual_setup_exception, stack overflow, no SERVING. Wine 9 and 10 were not tested. 11.0 is the version that worked here, not proof that every other Wine works. Do not use a distro wine package that installs Wine 8. Keep DedicatedServer next to bin/, GUI/ and SubModule.xml. Prefer host networking for UDP, and leave the console attached. SERVING does not need a GPU. It does need a display; Xvfb is enough, and some hosts need MIT-SHM off. Discord also mentions Ubuntu + Wine + winbind + Xvfb as a community note.
section.linux-notes.b10.d0.b0.0: bannerlordcoop-server-manager and the unofficial Pterodactyl egg are community tools. Read their source and check compatibility before you use them. This guide does not install them.
section.linux-notes.b10.summary.0: Community tools are not official support
section.linux-notes.b11.d0.b0.0: The official FAQ supports Linux and does not support Steam Deck. Deck reports differ: https://github.com/Bannerlord-Coop-Team/BannerlordCoop/issues/2162. Hosting and playing on one PC is estimated at 8 CPU cores and 16 GB of RAM. A separate dedicated server is the safer plan, and it does not need the game running. Linux stalls during character transfer are tracked in issue #2095.
section.linux-notes.b11.summary.0: What the FAQ says about Linux and hardware
section.linux-notes.b12.d0.b0.0: Compare the full Bannerlord build, not only the Co-op release. A small build difference can stall a join. Read the server log for the refused build or mod. Save, stop only that server, then back up CoopData and any server-data folder before you replace files. Do not unsubscribe, resubscribe or restart Steam during someone's session.
section.linux-notes.b12.summary.0: Match the full game build before you update
section.linux-notes.b13.d0.b0.0: Windows exit -1073741819 is an access violation. Check blocked or missing DLLs, and keep your save backups. -532462766 is an unhandled .NET exception. Exit 1 is generic. Exit 25 points at ProgramData/Mount and Blade II Bannerlord/logs/starter_log.txt inside the prefix. Read the lines above the number. These FAQ notes were not re-tested here.
section.linux-notes.b14.d0.b0.0: This guide uses the published Win64 binaries. Native .NET server work is tracked at https://github.com/Bannerlord-Coop-Team/BannerlordCoop/issues/2843. Seeing that repository does not let you build or redistribute the game. The TAOM client launcher is Windows-only and is reported not to work under Proton or Wine. Other mods are not guaranteed. Get Co-op working alone first.

metadata.title: Bannerlord Co-op on Linux
metadata.description: Host a Bannerlord Co-op server on Linux, then join from a matching client.
ui.copyFailed: Select the text and copy it
ui.startSub: Install and run Bannerlord Co-op on Linux.
ui.allStages: All install stages on one page.
nav.dSub: Pick your distribution. The guide will show only the commands for it.
distro.ubuntu.blurb: The most popular desktop Linux, with long-term releases and a huge package catalog.
distro.debian.blurb: The stable, community-run universal OS that Ubuntu and many others are built on.
distro.mint.blurb: A friendly, familiar Ubuntu-based desktop that works well out of the box.
distro.fedora.blurb: A fast-moving, upstream-first distro from Red Hat's community; RHEL-family systems use the same commands.
distro.arch.blurb: A rolling-release, do-it-yourself distro with the newest packages and the AUR.
distro.manjaro.blurb: An Arch-based rolling release with a friendlier installer and curated updates.
distro.suse.blurb: Tumbleweed (rolling) and Leap (stable) from the SUSE community, with zypper and YaST.
distro.bazzite.blurb: A gaming-ready immutable OS built on Fedora that updates as a single image (Silverblue-style systems fit here too).
distro.deck.blurb: Valve's handheld and its SteamOS: a read-only system, so use Desktop Mode and keep changes small.
distro.nix.blurb: A declarative, reproducible Linux that is configured entirely through Nix.
distro.other.name: Other distro
distro.other.blurb: Gentoo, Void, Alpine or anything else: you get the generic commands to adapt.
ui.oneScriptSub: One copy-paste script for your distro
ui.doneBody: Host from this machine, then join from a matching client.
